title: Students who play old-style jazz and learning tunes by ear
summary: Tulane students and a guest pianist play old-style jazz. Zanco learned tunes his mother hummed and plays entirely by ear because he cannot read music.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Old style clarinet, yeah. Old style piano. We had a fellow sat in with us just this past Sunday. I don't know his name. I don't know where he came from, but he was a pretty good pianist. And we did a version on Millenberg. And, I mean, this guy could really pawn a piano.
He sort of sounded like Duncan and Palmisano, you know, those guys.

I'm sorry I didn't catch his name. He'd probably come back up again. Well, just that type of music attracts them, they will be back, see, and they're going to want to play again. We're always glad to have them play.
But, now, that was not a young student type, so you'd expect him to play Old Style. He wasn't, no. Well, I mean. I'm surprised that there's that many students that play Old Style.

Well, surprised. You see, the way I figure this, the older people heard this music once before, and it's familiar to them. The newer people, the younger people, hadn't heard it, and it's something all together new to them, so that attracts them. And, well, the surprise is it is. I mean, some of these youngsters, I'd say, 18, 19 years old, can play some of these older tunes. Law knows they were way before these kids' time, but they know the tunes, you know, just as if they were brought up around the tune. They say, and they can play them.
Well, I know too much mustard, and I certainly wasn't around when that was popular.

Well, that's the same with me. Some of these tunes, I remember, well, my mother used to hum them, you see. Of course, at the time, I didn't know the name of the tune, but over a period of years, you know, you start fooling around, fooling around. You say, well, this might sound right, and you'll add this to the tune.
And before you know it, you actually piece that whole tune, and you're playing it just the way it was originally meant to be, you know.

Well, myself, I speak for myself, playing by ear like that, I mean, I have to rely on that, see. That's the only way I can play it. I have to hear it. If I heard it once before, I could play it, you know. But, it's, I'm at a disadvantage, of course, not being able to read music. I always said I would give my ride on if I could read music. But, I just have to rely on what I hear right now. It's kind of, you know, that old saying, you can't teach old dog new tricks. You know.
